{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wy-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"37fe732652e1fc99b3c8ae02f5c5e0e08190a7ef5310cc1be2e468d5e581e9e3","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wy-class-c:lineage:48","source_registry_sha256":"f2806994ac56e29c3588fb4e8e2cc870c5f64d0616933994765d31d7841ccbe9","source_liveness_sha256":"e9e98c5695424e30c400f1e14b2593178d09ca723f8f00581c9655dcae32ca6c"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Crashes, vehicle equipment and sharing the road — C.01","heading":"C — Crashes, vehicle equipment and sharing the road","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Crashes, vehicle equipment and sharing the road
FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
After a crash involving you, stop at or near the scene and remain until police arrive and question everyone involved. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
Give assistance to injured people and send for an ambulance after a crash. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A01
Do not move an injured person unless another crash poses a danger. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A01
Warn approaching traffic after a crash to prevent additional harm. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A01
Obtain names and addresses for the witnesses and the people involved in the crash. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A01
Record the other driver's name, address and driver-license number. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A01
Record the other vehicle's make, model, year, damage and license-plate number. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A01
Record the other driver's insurance-company name. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A01
Contact police for a crash involving injury, death or at least $1,000 of property damage. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A01
Provide police with crash information at the time of the crash. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A01
Police complete and submit the crash report to WYDOT's Accident Records Section. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A01
If unattended property is damaged and its owner cannot be found, leave a note where the owner can find it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A01
That unattended-property note must include your name, address, telephone, driver-license number and license-plate number. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A01
The unattended-property note must also state the crash date, time and vehicle damage. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A01
After leaving the unattended-property information, also contact the nearest law-enforcement agency. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A02
A police officer may stop and inspect vehicle equipment, require immediate repair of defects and issue a fine if the vehicle is unsafe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A02
Required headlights, parking lights, brake lights, tail lights and turn signals must work properly. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A02
The vehicle's brakes and parking brake must be in good operating condition. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A02
Required mirrors, horn and safety belts must function properly. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A02
The required windshield, wipers, tires, muffler and exhaust system must be in good condition. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A02
Use the recommended tire pressure from the vehicle owner's manual or driver-side door jamb. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A02
Measure tire pressure with a tire-pressure gauge. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A02
If measured pressure is above the door-jamb recommendation, release air until it matches. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F24 | anchor: A02
If pressure is below the vehicle recommendation, add air or seek tire-professional help to reach it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F25 | anchor: A02
Inspect tires for wear and damage monthly or before a long road trip. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F26 | anchor: A02
For the penny-test setup, hold the coin at Lincoln's body and insert his head into a groove where tread appears lowest. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F27 | anchor: A03
In the handbook's penny test, tread covering any part of Lincoln's head is the stated pass criterion. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F28 | anchor: A03
Tread below the penny-test criterion reduces grip in adverse conditions. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F29 | anchor: A03
Motorcyclists share the rights and responsibilities of other public-road users. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F30 | anchor: A03
A motorcycle can be difficult to identify in traffic, and its distance or speed can be hard to judge. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F31 | anchor: A03
Before turning left ahead of an approaching motorcycle, look again and establish its speed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F32 | anchor: A03
Do not enter ahead of a signaling motorcycle until you know the rider is actually turning rather than continuing straight. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F33 | anchor: A03
Most motorcycle turn signals do not cancel automatically. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F34 | anchor: A03
A motorcycle is entitled to the full lane, so never move alongside it in the same lane even when the lane is wide or the rider is near one side. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F35 | anchor: A03
Motorcyclists may change position within a lane to see, be seen or avoid objects near the road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F36 | anchor: A03
Bad weather, slick pavement, crosswinds, rail crossings, metal bridges and grooves may cause a motorcycle to change speed or direction quickly. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F37 | anchor: A04
Yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk area even when no pavement markings are present. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F38 | anchor: A04
Near schools, slow down and enlarge the space cushion when pedestrians are present. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F39 | anchor: A04
Children near residential or school traffic may run into a vehicle's path unexpectedly. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F40 | anchor: A04
If a disabled vehicle forces you to walk where there is no sidewalk, walk on the road's left side facing traffic. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F41 | anchor: A04
Wear light-colored clothing when walking at night so drivers can see you more easily. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F42 | anchor: A04
Bicyclists share the public-road rights and duties of vehicle drivers and must ride as near the pavement's right side as practical and safe. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F43 | anchor: A04
Although a car may legally travel beside a bicycle in one lane, the handbook advises leaving more room instead. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F44 | anchor: A04
A cyclist may swerve to avoid a grate, road object or opening car door, so leave ample room while following or passing. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F45 | anchor: A04
A bicycle used after dark must have a front light and rear reflectors, which can still be difficult for drivers to see. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F46 | anchor: A04
Watch the road edge for bicycles at night rather than relying only on their lights and reflectors. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0070]

Misconceptions: A visible motorcycle turn signal does not prove the rider is turning, and a truck's elevated cab does not eliminate blind spots.

Glossary: Recall terms: unattended property, tire-pressure gauge, full lane, slow-moving vehicle, roadside warning signal and wildlife collision.
Dynamic facts: Phone numbers, rider-course availability and undated crash proportions are withheld. Source-currency and differing Move Over summaries remain explicit debt.
